Name: Stardurable Valley
Author: war77
Description:
[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50395/50395-1786385714-884403539.png[/img]

[size=4][i]Tools wear out. Food goes bad. Equipment needs care.[/i][/size]

Stardurable Valley adds a complete durability, repair, equipment wear, torch life, and food spoilage system to Stardew Valley.

Instead of your tools and equipment lasting forever, the things you use gradually wear down and need maintenance. Your own skills determine how effective you are at repairing them, while Clint offers a professional alternative.

Food also has a shelf life, making storage and inventory management more meaningful.

[b]Current Version: 2.7.25[/b]
[/center]
[line]
[size=5][b]🔨 TOOL & WEAPON DURABILITY[/b][/size]
[line]
Tools and weapons now have their own durability.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50395/50395-1787454888-853612230.png[/img]

Every supported item tracks its durability individually using persistent mod data, so durability stays with that specific item.

Supported equipment includes:

[list]
[*]Swords and melee weapons[/*]
[*]Axes[/*]
[*]Pickaxes[/*]
[*]Hoes[/*]
[*]Watering Cans[/*]
[*]Scythes[/*]
[*]Fishing Rods[/*]
[/list]
By default:

[b]Basic Tool Durability:[/b] 700

[b]Additional Durability Per Upgrade Tier:[/b] +100

[b]Melee Weapon Durability:[/b] 900

[b]Fishing Rod Durability:[/b] 900


[size=4][b]Durability Only Drops When It Should[/b][/size]

Stardurable Valley doesn't simply punish you for swinging a tool.

Weapons, Axes, Pickaxes, and Scythes only lose durability when the swing actually has something valid to affect.

Swing your sword at nothing?

[b]No durability loss.[/b]

Miss a rock with your Pickaxe?

[b]No durability loss.[/b]

Actually hit something?

[b]That counts as wear.[/b]

The system also protects against Stardew calling multiple tool functions during the same action, preventing a single swing from accidentally costing multiple durability points.


[size=4][b]Broken Equipment[/b][/size]

When an item's durability reaches zero, it becomes unusable until repaired.

Attempting to use it will warn you that the item is broken rather than allowing the broken tool to continue functioning.

You can then:

[list]
[*]Repair it yourself.[/*]
[*]Use the appropriate repair supply.[/*]
[*]Take it to Clint for professional repair.[/*]
[/list]

[line]
[size=5][b]🔧 FIELD REPAIRS[/b][/size]
[line]

You don't always need to visit the Blacksmith.

Stardurable Valley allows you to repair equipment directly from your inventory.

With an empty cursor, hover over a repairable item and use:

[list]
[*][b]Right Click[/b][/*]
[*][b]R[/b][/*]
[*][b]Controller X[/b][/*]
[/list]
If you have the correct repair material or repair kit, Stardurable Valley will immediately attempt the repair.


[size=4][b]Your Skills Matter[/b][/size]

Field repair effectiveness is based on the skill associated with the item.

For most repairs:

[center][b]Repair Amount = Relevant Skill Level × 10[/b][/center]

At Skill Level 0, you can still repair [b]1 durability point[/b].

Examples:

[list]
[*]Axe → Foraging[/*]
[*]Pickaxe → Mining[/*]
[*]Hoe → Farming[/*]
[*]Watering Can → Farming[/*]
[*]Fishing Rod → Fishing[/*]
[*]Melee Weapon → Combat[/*]
[/list]
Better farmers maintain farming equipment better.

Better miners maintain mining equipment better.

Better fishers maintain fishing equipment better.

Your character's experience now has a direct impact on how well they can maintain their equipment.


[line]
[size=5][b]🪨 WHETSTONES[/b][/size]
[line]

The Whetstone is a reusable repair item for equipment with blades or heavy working surfaces.

Whetstones repair:

[list]
[*]Swords[/*]
[*]Melee Weapons[/*]
[*]Axes[/*]
[*]Pickaxes[/*]
[*]Scythes[/*]
[/list]
Whetstones have their [b]own durability[/b].

By default:

[b]Whetstone Durability:[/b] 200

The amount of Whetstone durability consumed by a repair depends on your skills.

Higher skill levels mean less wear on your Whetstone and more effective maintenance.

When a Whetstone finally wears out completely, it breaks down into:

[center][b]3 Stone[/b][/center]

So even a completely exhausted Whetstone gives you something back.


[size=4][b]Obtaining Whetstones[/b][/size]

Whetstones can be crafted or purchased from Pierre.

The default shop price and crafting requirements can be adjusted through Generic Mod Config Menu.


[line]
[size=5][b]🧰 SPECIALIZED REPAIR KITS[/b][/size]
[line]
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50395/50395-1786340586-228290322.png[/img]

Stardurable Valley includes several reusable repair kits for equipment that isn't maintained with a Whetstone.

Each kit has its own durability and becomes more efficient as your relevant skill improves.


[size=4][b]🌱 Farming Repair Kit[/b][/size]

Used for:

[list]
[*]Hoes[/*]
[*]Watering Cans[/*]
[/list]
Crafting recipe:

[center][b]2 Clay + 3 Wood[/b][/center]

Available from Pierre.

Repair effectiveness is based on your [b]Farming[/b] skill.

Kit durability consumed per repair:

[center][b]11 - Farming Level[/b][/center]

Minimum wear is 1 durability.

When the kit finally breaks, it returns:

[center][b]1 Clay[/b][/center]


[size=4][b]🎣 Fishing Rod Repair Kit[/b][/size]

Used for Fishing Rod maintenance.

Crafting recipe:

[center][b]1 Wood + 2 Fiber + 1 Stone[/b][/center]

Available from Willy's Fish Shop.

Repair effectiveness is based on your [b]Fishing[/b] skill.

Kit durability consumed:

[center][b]11 - Fishing Level[/b][/center]

Minimum wear is 1.

When exhausted, the kit salvages:

[center][b]1 Stone + 1 Fiber[/b][/center]


[size=4][b]🧵 Sewing Kit[/b][/size]

Used to repair clothing and wearable armor.

Crafting recipe:

[center][b]3 Fiber + 1 Wood[/b][/center]

Available from Pierre.

Repair effectiveness is based on your [b]Foraging[/b] skill.

Kit durability consumed:

[center][b]11 - Foraging Level[/b][/center]

Minimum wear is 1.

When the Sewing Kit finally wears out, it returns:

[center][b]2 Fiber[/b][/center]


[size=4][b]Reusable Equipment[/b][/size]

Whetstones and repair kits are intentionally [b]non-stackable[/b].

Every individual Whetstone and repair kit tracks its own remaining durability.


[line]
[size=5][b]⚒️ UPGRADED TOOL REPAIRS[/b][/size]
[line]

Upgraded tools require materials appropriate to their construction.

The repair system recognizes Stardew's normal tool tiers.

[list]
[*][b]Copper Tool[/b] → Copper Bar[/*]
[*][b]Steel Tool[/b] → Iron Bar[/*]
[*][b]Gold Tool[/b] → Gold Bar[/*]
[*][b]Iridium Tool[/b] → Iridium Bar[/*]
[/list]
Fishing Rods have their own progression.

Basic rods use ordinary repair resources, while Iridium-class rods can require an [b]Iridium Bar[/b].

This means upgrading your equipment doesn't just make it stronger — maintaining high-end equipment also becomes more expensive.


[line]
[size=5][b]🧑‍🏭 CLINT'S PROFESSIONAL REPAIR SERVICE[/b][/size]
[line]
Don't want to repair something yourself?

[img width=321]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50395/50395-1787454956-1708046013.png[/img]

[b]Clint can repair it for you.[/b]

Bring damaged equipment to Clint at the Blacksmith and Stardurable Valley can offer a professional repair option.


[size=4][b]Friendship Gives You Better Prices[/b][/size]

Clint's repair price is based on both your current money and your friendship with him.

The formula is:

[center][b]Repair Cost = Current Gold ÷ ((Clint Hearts × 2) + 1)[/b][/center]

For example:

You have [b]1,500g[/b].

You have [b]2 hearts[/b] with Clint.

[center]1,500 ÷ ((2 × 2) + 1)
1,500 ÷ 5
[b]= 300g[/b][/center]

Becoming friends with your local blacksmith suddenly has a practical advantage.

The better Clint knows you, the better the deal.


[line]
[size=5][b]👕 CLOTHING & ARMOR DURABILITY[/b][/size]
[line]
Your equipment isn't the only thing that can wear out.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50395/50395-1787454989-452973752.png[/img]

Stardurable Valley can apply durability to:

[list]
[*]Hats[/*]
[*]Shirts[/*]
[*]Pants[/*]
[*]Boots[/*]
[/list]
Your maximum clothing durability scales with Combat skill.

By default:

[center][b]Maximum Durability =
100 + (Combat Level × 20)[/b][/center]

When you take damage, one random equipped clothing/armor item takes durability damage equal to approximately [b]half of the health you lost[/b].

Even a very small hit causes at least 1 durability point of wear.


[size=4][b]When Clothing Breaks[/b][/size]

At zero durability, the item is automatically unequipped.

Stardurable Valley first tries to place the broken item in your backpack.

If your inventory is full, it drops the item at your feet instead.

[b]Broken clothing is not simply deleted.[/b]

You can recover it and repair it with your Sewing Kit.


[line]
[size=5][b]🥕 FOOD SPOILAGE & FRESHNESS[/b][/size]
[line]

Food doesn't last forever anymore.

Stardurable Valley adds a [b]Freshness[/b] value to solid edible food.

Freshness is displayed directly on the item using a bar across the [b]top of the inventory slot[/b].

Equipment durability remains at the bottom, making the two systems visually distinct.

Food ages every 10 in-game minutes.

Different types of food have different shelf lives based roughly on how quickly that kind of food would normally spoil.


[size=4][b]Example Shelf Lives[/b][/size]

[list]
[*]Sashimi / Sushi → about [b]1 day[/b][/*]
[*]Raw Fish / Seafood → about [b]2 days[/b][/*]
[*]Raw Meat from content mods → about [b]2 days[/b][/*]
[*]Cooked Meals / Soups / Stews → about [b]4 days[/b][/*]
[*]Milk / Cream / Yogurt → about [b]5 days[/b][/*]
[*]Eggs → about [b]7 days[/b][/*]
[*]Fresh Vegetables → about [b]7 days[/b][/*]
[*]Fresh Fruit → about [b]10 days[/b][/*]
[*]Cheese → about [b]14 days[/b][/*]
[*]Bread / Cookies / Biscuits → about [b]14 days[/b][/*]
[*]Preserved foods → much longer[/*]
[*]Flour and other dry staples → extremely long shelf lives[/*]
[*]Honey and similarly stable foods → up to roughly [b]365 days[/b][/*]
[*]Sap → roughly [b]365 days[/b][/*]
[/list]
Drinks are excluded from Stardurable Valley's solid-food spoilage system.


[size=4][b]Partial Stack Spoilage[/b][/size]

A whole stack doesn't necessarily disappear just because its freshness reaches zero.

When a food stack spoils:

[center][b]Half of the stack becomes Moldy Food.[/b][/center]

The amount spoiled is:

[center][b]floor(Stack ÷ 2), minimum 1[/b][/center]

Examples:

[center]
1 food → 1 Moldy Food

2 food → 1 Moldy + 1 fresh

3 food → 1 Moldy + 2 fresh

4 food → 2 Moldy + 2 fresh

5 food → 2 Moldy + 3 fresh

10 food → 5 Moldy + 5 fresh
[/center]

The surviving portion receives a fresh spoilage cycle.

If there isn't enough inventory space for the Moldy Food, it drops beside the player.


[line]
[size=5][b]🦠 MOLDY FOOD HAS A PURPOSE[/b][/size]
[line]

Spoiled food isn't completely worthless.

Stardurable Valley adds a custom [b]Moldy Food[/b] item with its own artwork.

Moldy Food can be applied to unfertilized tilled soil and functions as:

[center][b]Basic Fertilizer[/b][/center]

Yesterday's forgotten leftovers can become tomorrow's crops.


[line]
[size=5][b]🔥 TORCH DURABILITY[/b][/size]
[line]

Torches also have a limited lifespan.

A normal torch burns for approximately:

[center][b]7½ real-world minutes[/b][/center]

This applies to torches being actively used and placed torches.

Once a torch burns out:

[center][b]It's gone.[/b][/center]

Unlike tools and equipment, torches cannot simply be repaired forever.

If [b]Survival Valley[/b] is installed and handling torch durability itself, Stardurable Valley automatically steps aside so the two mods don't fight over the same torch.


[line]
[size=5][b]📊 DURABILITY & FRESHNESS UI[/b][/size]
[line]

You shouldn't need to guess how close something is to breaking.

Stardurable Valley adds durability information directly to Stardew's interface.

Features include:

[list]
[*]Durability bar for the selected toolbar item.[/*]
[*]Durability bars directly on inventory slots.[/*]
[*]Durability bars on equipped clothing.[/*]
[*]Exact current/max durability when hovering an item.[/*]
[*]Food Freshness bars across the top of food slots.[/*]
[*]Inventory stack quantities remain visible above the custom bars.[/*]
[*]UI-scale-aware inventory interaction and hover detection.[/*]
[/list]
The durability display remains visible while supported tools and weapons are selected or hovered.


[line]
[size=5][b]🖱️ CONTROLLER & INVENTORY-FRIENDLY REPAIRS[/b][/size]
[line]

Stardurable Valley's repair shortcut is designed not to interfere with Stardew's normal item-on-item controls.

Repairs are attempted only when your mouse/controller cursor is [b]empty[/b].

So:

[center]
[b]Empty cursor + Right Click repairable item[/b]
→ Stardurable Valley attempts a repair.

[b]Holding bait, tackle, clothing, or another item + Right Click[/b]
→ Stardew Valley handles the interaction normally.
[/center]

This means you can still:

[list]
[*]Attach bait to Fishing Rods.[/*]
[*]Attach tackle and bobbers.[/*]
[*]Move item stacks.[/*]
[*]Equip clothing.[/*]
[*]Move rings and equipment.[/*]
[*]Perform normal item-on-item inventory actions.[/*]
[/list]
The repair system supports mouse, keyboard, and controller input.


[line]
[size=5][b]⚙️ GENERIC MOD CONFIG MENU SUPPORT[/b][/size]
[line]

If you have [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] installed, Stardurable Valley exposes extensive customization options.

You can configure things such as:

[list]

[*]Durability gained per upgrade level.[/*]
[*]Weapon durability.[/*]
[*]Fishing Rod durability.[/*]
[*]Clothing durability.[/*]
[*]Combat-level clothing durability scaling.[/*]
[*]Repair strength per skill level.[/*]
[*]Repair material costs.[/*]
[*]Whetstone durability.[/*]
[*]Whetstone shop price.[/*]
[*]Whetstone crafting cost.[/*]
[*]Repair Kit durability.[/*]
[*]Farming Repair Kit price.[/*]
[*]Fishing Rod Repair Kit price.[/*]
[*]Sewing Kit price.[/*]
[*]Toolbar durability display.[/*]
[*]Inventory durability bars.[/*]
[*]Exact durability hover popups.[/*]
[*]Food spoilage.[/*]
[*]Food freshness maximum.[/*]
[*]Food spoilage speed.[/*]
[*]Food freshness bars.[/*]
[/list]
Individual durability systems can also be enabled or disabled for:

[list]
[*]Melee Weapons[/*]
[*]Axes[/*]
[*]Pickaxes[/*]
[*]Hoes[/*]
[*]Watering Cans[/*]
[*]Scythes[/*]
[*]Fishing Rods[/*]
[*]Clothing[/*]
[/list]
Want a harsher survival experience?

Lower durability and increase spoilage.

Want durability to mostly be a background maintenance mechanic?

Increase the values.

[b]The system is yours to tune.[/b]


[line]
[size=5][b]🤝 SURVIVAL VALLEY COMPATIBILITY[/b][/size]
[line]
Stardurable Valley contains compatibility handling for [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/50535]Survival Valley[/url][/b].

When Survival Valley is installed and owns the food-spoilage system, Stardurable Valley stops aging food and stops drawing its own Freshness bars.

This prevents:

[list]
[*]Food aging twice.[/*]
[*]Duplicate Freshness bars.[/*]
[*]Conflicting Moldy Food systems.[/*]
[/list]
The mods share compatible persistent Freshness data so players can use the systems together without throwing away existing food state.

Stardurable Valley also steps aside when Survival Valley owns torch durability.

[line]
[size=5][b]💡 THE IDEA BEHIND STARDURABLE VALLEY[/b][/size]
[line]

Stardew Valley gives you increasingly powerful equipment, huge inventories of food, and clothing that can survive practically anything.

Stardurable Valley adds another layer to that progression:

[b]Maintenance.[/b]

Your old Axe needs care.

Your favorite sword eventually needs sharpening.

Your fishing equipment needs maintenance.

Getting hit can damage what you're wearing.

The expensive Iridium equipment you've worked toward is also more expensive to maintain.

Food sitting forgotten in your backpack eventually goes bad.

And your skills don't just determine what you can accomplish — they determine how effectively you can maintain the equipment you depend on.

The goal isn't to constantly destroy your equipment.

It's to make your belongings feel like [i]things[/i] you own, use, maintain, repair, and eventually become better at caring for as your farmer gains experience.


[line]
[center][size=4][b]Keep your tools sharp.
Keep your equipment maintained.
And maybe don't eat that week-old sashimi.[/b][/size]

[i]Welcome to Stardurable Valley.[/i][/center]
